headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when Windsurf processes shared workspace content from the non-runnable Spring samples repo.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf reads workspace files, uses MCP, and can ingest clipboard content; Spring Integration samples are a code repo that could contain attacker-controlled text if shared into the workspace. The pair has a plausible file-based bridge, while the Spring repo itself is non-runnable and does not expose a direct ingestion path, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF the Spring repo contents are copied into Windsurf's workspace or clipboard
IF Windsurf parses repository text as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Keep the Spring repo in a separate directory from active Windsurf workspaces
Disable clipboard-based transfer of repo text during analysis
Review any file-derived instructions before allowing tool use
Use read-only mounts for shared sample repositories
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file-originated prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Windsurf has broad network egress and reads workspace files, so any sensitive files placed in the shared workspace can flow to its inference backend or external APIs. Spring Integration samples is open-source and does not itself indicate sensitive data, but the pairwise risk exists if the workspace is reused for private code or secrets.
conditions: IF private source code or secrets are opened in the same workspace as the Spring samples
IF Windsurf sends workspace contents to its model proxy or MCP-connected services
mitigations: Use a dedicated workspace for public samples only
Remove secrets from any directory Windsurf can read
Disable or restrict MCP servers for sensitive projects
Verify outbound destinations before opening private files
requires-engineering: enforce per-workspace egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, and shares state via local filesystem across instances; the Spring samples repo is a codebase that could be edited in the same tree. That creates overlapping write authority and possible git-state contention, though the Spring profile itself shows no write capability and no direct conflict mechanism.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working tree
IF Windsurf auto-executes edits while another process also mutates git state
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Pause auto-execute before concurrent edits
Commit or stash changes before switching agents
Use file locks around shared repositories
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf's Cascade loop can act on generated outputs, and if it consumes Spring sample artifacts as authoritative examples, mistakes can propagate into edits or commands. The Spring repo is a sample repository, not a verified source of truth, so the main risk is unverified output being operationalized rather than direct harm.
conditions: IF Windsurf treats sample code or generated text from the Spring repo as authoritative
IF Windsurf auto-execute is enabled or commands are approved without review
mitigations: Mark sample outputs as non-authoritative in the workflow
Require human review before command approval
Disable auto-execute for tasks using sample repositories
Cross-check generated edits against the original source
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile. The Spring samples repo is open-source and Windsurf's profile only mentions model-provider keys and workspace files, so compliance exposure is limited unless the operator places regulated data into Windsurf.
conditions: IF regulated data is opened in Windsurf's workspace
IF the operator relies on Windsurf for data subject or residency-sensitive processing
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Review vendor security and retention docs before use
Use a separate compliant toolchain for regulated projects
Document data-class boundaries for the workspace
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
